rv.q: Michael Crawford returns to the West End, after a five-year break, in a piece that’s appreciably different from the kind of shows (Barnum, The Phantom of the Opera) that rocketed him to stardom.

As delicate as it is delightful, The Go-Between isn’t going to be to everyone’s tastes. But it is a quiet triumph of determination and a true labour of love that, five years after its regional premiere under the developmental umbrella of Perfect Pitch, has finally arrived in the West End.

Michael Crawford is back in the West End in a major musical role for the first time in a decade (yes, he was in, and starred as, The Wizard of Oz at the Palladium five years ago but he didn’t, as here, “carry” the show.) I wish I could say “rejoice”, hang out the bunting and convene a street party along Shaftesbury Avenue.
